According to the participant, she had experienced a 3‑day history of headache prior to admission, followed by lower abdominal pain, back pain, unilateral/generalized side pain, and absence of fetal movements one day before presenting to the facility. These symptoms progressed, prompting her to seek care.
On admission (17 February 2026), facility assessment reportedly confirmed intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD). 
The participant was admitted and managed for IUFD. Labour was induced using Cytotec 200 mcg PV, followed by Cytotec 100 mcg slow release every 3 hours. She delivered on 19 February 2026 after a total labour duration of 8 hours 55 minutes. The outcome was a macerated stillbirth at 27 weeks + 6 days gestation.

column13:
This serious adverse event involves a 32-year-old pregnant participant enrolled in the study on 10 February 2026  who subsequently experienced intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD) at 27+6 weeks gestation. The participant initially met eligibility due to symptoms consistent with suspected preeclampsia (headache and visual disturbances) but was clinically stable at enrolment with no proteinuria and unremarkable systemic findings.
The participant missed her scheduled Visit 2 and became unreachable despite repeated follow-up attempts. On 22 February 2026, she informed the study team that she had been admitted at Parirenyatwa facility on 17 February 2026 following worsening symptoms, including a 3‑day history of headache, lower abdominal pain, flank pain, and absence of fetal movements. Clinical assessment at the facility on admission confirmed intrauterine fetal demise. Laboratory results showed elevated WCC (16.7) with normal haemoglobin (12 g/dL) and platelet count (359). She was admitted and managed for IUFD, undergoing induction of labour with Cytotec, leading to delivery of a macerated stillbirth on 19 February 2026 after 8 hours 55 minutes of labour.
The event meets seriousness criteria due to fetal death and hospitalization and was promptly reported to regulatory authorities per protocol requirements. Causality is unlikely linked to study participation or procedures

Review of source documents subsequently confirmed that the participant’s dating ultrasound performed on 15 January 2026 indicated a gestational age of 16 weeks and 3 days, corresponding to approximately 19 weeks’ gestation at the time of enrollment.

Review of source documents subsequently confirmed that the participant’s dating ultrasound performed on 15 January 2026 indicated a gestational age of 16 weeks and 3 days, corresponding to approximately 19 weeks’ gestation at the time of enrollment.

The participant missed Visit 2, which had been scheduled for 19 February 2026. The study team made multiple unsuccessful attempts to contact her following the missed visit.
On 23 February 2026, contact was established, and the participant reported that she had gone into labour. She confirmed that she had delivered her baby, and that the newborn had been admitted to the nursery for respiratory distress.
The infant was hospitalised for three days and received oxygen therapy. The baby subsequently recovered and was discharged.
As neonatal hospitalization meets criteria for a Serious Adverse Event (SAE), this note serves as the initial SAE report.
